name: Romanesco

ancestors.notes: Re-Tuscanised since 15th c.: modern Romanesco is heavily influenced by standard Italian.

notes: Romanesco (Roman dialect). Central Italian of Rome and Lazio. Historically distinct from Tuscan, but re-Tuscanised from the 15th century onward due to the Papal court. Key features: (1) NO gorgia. (2) Rhotacism: /l/ → [r] before consonants (alto → [ˈarto]). (3) -ND- → [nː], -MB- → [mː]. (4) Affricate strengthening: /dʒ/ → [dːʒ] intervocalically. Literary tradition from Belli (19th c.) (D'Achille & Giovanardi 2001). GRAPHEMES: the grapheme table and its positional readings come from it-IT through graphemes_base, because the variety writes standard Italian spelling. ⟨c g⟩ read [tʃ dʒ] before ⟨e i⟩ and [k ɡ] elsewhere: cielo [ˈtʃɛːlo], gelo [ˈdʒɛːlo] (Bertinetto & Loporcaro 2005, JIPA 35(2), p. 133). ⟨i u⟩ before a vowel are the glides [j w]: pieno [ˈpjɛːno], chiave [ˈkjaːve], guida [ˈɡwiːda] (p. 139, Table 2 on p. 138). The spec keeps its own ⟨s⟩ and ⟨z⟩ readings and does not take the it-IT positional ones. 'Intervocalic /s/ is voiceless in RI, so that SI minimal pairs, such as [ˈkjɛːse] ‘asked.3sg’ vs. [ˈkjɛːze] ‘churches’ (both spelled chiese), are neutralised as [ˈkjɛːse] in RI' (p. 133). The it-IT word-initial [dz] for ⟨z⟩ has no Roman source here, so ⟨z⟩ keeps [ts] first.

sources.author: Bertinetto, P.M. & Loporcaro, M.
sources.title: The sound pattern of Standard Italian, as compared with the varieties spoken in Florence, Milan and Rome
sources.publisher: Journal of the International Phonetic Association
sources.notes: JIPA 35(2). Illustration of Standard Italian; states the preconsonantal /s/ voicing agreement and documents the Tuscan/Northern split in intervocalic ⟨s⟩. Table 2 (p. 138) and p. 139 give the opening and closing diphthongs and the hiatus that the stress diphthongs list follows; p. 137 gives the two equal vowels in hiatus.
